chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, who said:

I wrote to him that our companions have differed regarding us, so some of them said that the departure on the last day after midday is superior, and some of them said before midday. So he wrote: Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed Dhuhr and Asr in Mecca, and that could not happen unless he had departed before midday?

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: Midday (when the sun passes its zenith)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred time for departing Mina during Hajj according to the Prophet's practice?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* resolves the juristic dispute among companions regarding the optimal timing for departing Mina by appealing to the Prophet’s established practice (Sunnah). The Imam demonstrates that since the Prophet combined Dhuhr and Asr in Mea, he must have departed before the sun reached its zenith (zawal), thereby establishing the precedence of early departure as a normative act of following the Prophet's example. This ruling underscores the Shia method of deriving legal preferences from the practical implementation of the Prophet's rituals rather than mere textual speculation.
